question: A patient with alcoholic cirrhosis has: serum bilirubin 3.2 mg/dL, albumin 2.8 g/dL, INR 1.9, grade II hepatic encephalopathy, and moderate ascites. What is the Child-Pugh class?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Child-Pugh A requires a low total score (5–6). This patient has bilirubin 3.2 (2 pts), albumin 2.8 (2 pts), INR 1.9 (2 pts), grade II HE (3 pts), and moderate ascites (2 pts) = 11 points.
Incorrect. The score totals 11, which exceeds the Child-Pugh B range of 7–9.
Correct. Bilirubin 3.2 mg/dL = 2 pts, albumin 2.8 g/dL = 2 pts, INR 1.9 = 2 pts, grade II encephalopathy = 3 pts, moderate ascites = 2 pts — total 11 = Child-Pugh C. 1-year survival ~45%.
Incorrect. The score is 11, placing this patient firmly in Child-Pugh C, not on the A–B boundary.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the five Child-Pugh parameters (bilirubin, albumin, INR, encephalopathy grade, ascites) and their point allocations: each scored 1–3 points; classes A=5–6, B=7–9, C=10–15.
Well done. Systematic scoring of all five Child-Pugh parameters places this patient in class C, indicating decompensated cirrhosis.
